MID_c030_0280g_01100_00050_0: The man's research came from a place of love for his younger brother, who was born unable to walk. Prosthetic redesign was a technology that replaced a person's limbs with machinery that could be controlled like a flesh-and-blood arm or leg, and as his research began to show promise, people started to take notice. Before he knew it, the man was being recruited to work at the royal research institute. Under the naive elief that the government only wanted to help others as he did, he accepted the position—a decision he would regret to his dying day. Soon, the research he had devoted his life to had become a source of pain, terror, and suffering for people beyond counting. I need to act! he thinks as he gazes up to the sky. His hand trembles as it presses against the gaping wound in his stomach, which has been torn apart by a rampaging victim. Next time, I'll put a stop to this war and save everyone!
MID_c030_0280g_01200_00050_0: As a rich man strolls through a dilapidated ruin outside the city, he stumbles upon a young Goat Person hovering near the brink of death. Though he mocks her internally, he offers her a small heel of bread on a whim, but the girl shakes her head weakly and refuses. Curious now, the man holds out a handful of coin, but she does not accept this gift either. With this, his bemusement turns to irritation. He is a man of money and status—and a man with everything a person could possibly desire. So how can this...this Goat Person possibly refuse him!? "What is it you want, Goat?" he asks. After a moment, she lifts her head and says in a trembling voice: "I...want you to stay with me." With that, she breathes her last. The man stares at her for a bit before turning on his heel and heading home. But that night, the man has a dream wherein a terrible monster that oozes malice stands before him. "What is it you want?" growls the beast. "My life!" cries the man. "I don't need anything so long as I have that!" Without hesitation, the monster lifts its fearsome claws and tears the man in half, only to find him completely empty inside.
MID_c030_0280g_01300_00050_0:
"Goodbye... Goodbye..."

The forest is still, save for the faint repeated words of farewell.
The girl with white hair parts the foliage, pressing closer to the
voice. As she does so, she spies a mechanical creature with
stubby limbs digging in the earth.
Beside it is the body of an identical-looking machine—a fallen
comrade patiently awaiting burial.

The girl knows a thing or two about the machines,
so she walks over to the operational one and offers to repair
its friend. But the machine continues to dig,
pausing only to murmur five words:

"WE ONLY HAVE ONE LIFE."

And as the girl looks at the flowers lying beside the broken
machine, she still does not understand the emotions that swirl
about inside her chest.
MID_c030_0280g_01400_00050_0:
In the schoolyard, budding mages—including a girl with wavy
hair and a girl with glasses—listen to their professor's lecture.
The instructor points at a spider sitting in the middle of a
dew-covered web before casting a spell that transforms it into
a beautiful butterfly. The creature flutters its brilliant wings and
prepares to take flight, only to realize it is trapped in the
selfsame web it so recently called its home.

"Turn it back," says the girl with wavy hair.
But the professor only shakes her head and explains that the
transformation of a living creature is an irreversible process.

"That's sort of terrifying," the girl with wavy hair whispers to
the bespectacled girl.

"I don't know," replies the other girl quietly.
"Maybe the spider is happy it got to experience freedom,
even if only for a moment."

As they watch, the butterfly writhes and twists within the
gossamer strands of silk before at last falling still.
MID_c030_0280g_01500_00050_0:
Though the laboratory is cramped and dim,
the woman inside has found the
answer humanity has so
desperately been seeking.
If she can put her results to use,
they can finally vanquish the
horror of the Flowers and
put an end to their seemingly endless war.

And yet, the emotion that takes
root in her heart is not joy,
but pain. For she knows that if her
research is successful,
she will never see him again.
Without Flowers,
the cloned soldiers that fight against
them are beings without
purpose—beings that would
doubtless be eliminated in short
order. In essence, a world without
Flowers is a world where her
own cloned self—as well as her
beloved husband—would
cease to exist.

And so she deletes the results
of her experiment,
rejecting the possibility of a peaceful
world in favor of one where
she and her husband fight in a war without end.

MID_c030_0280g_01600_00050_0: A flare from a distant camp illuminates the barracks in the night. Shadows of soldiers enjoying a laugh and a chat extend across the grassy plain. They speak of what they want to do when the war ends. How they will see their families—their lovers. How they will go to school and start new and better lives. And as their captain passes by, his men all ask him the same question: What will you do when the war is over? Each time, he shakes his head and brushes the question aside. His place is on the battlefield—for he once lost his own comrades, and now plans to stand forever in the midst of battle for the sake of those who will never return. In this way, he hopes to continue atoning for a sin he knows to be beyond forgiveness. The sound of artillery draws closer; when morning dawns, this area will become a killing field. Soldiers will set upon one another—kill one another compounding sin upon sin. But such is simply the way of things that have moved beyond the point of no return—a point achieved both in this war, and in the captain's heart.

PID_c070_2050b_03900_02130_1: WILL... THIS DESIRE I HAVE TO BE WITH SARYU—IS THAT MAKING ME STRONGER?
PID_c070_2050b_04000_02120_1: It is. People oftentimes find new strength just by being with those they hold dear.
PID_c070_2050b_04100_03220_1: That sort of fleeting strength will only leave you empty once it's gone.
PID_c070_2050b_04200_02120_1: You must have known how this felt a long time ago, didn't you?
PID_c070_2050b_04400_01060_1: We're all the same—we all have people dear to us. But I couldn't protect him...
PID_c070_2050b_04500_02140_1: I, too, left behind those I was meant to protect when I let go of my duty.
PID_c070_2050b_04600_02060_1: I believed I would get home, so I never doubted for a moment...
PID_c070_2050b_04700_03220_1: Exactly. You've all lost people, just like Her. Which means—
PID_c070_2050b_04800_01060_1: But even if the dark days seem endless, there's always a light at the end!
PID_c070_2050b_04800_03220_1: No! The dark never lifted. And that's why...that's why I want this world to—
PID_c070_2050b_05100_01060_1: Fio, Levania...we send our feelings to you!
PID_c070_2050b_05500_03220_1: This hardly matches up to the righteousness She carried.
PID_c070_2050b_05600_01050_1: I don't think it's about which one is more right.
PID_c070_2050b_05700_01040_1: That's right. Your pain, our hope—they're fine left the way they are.
PID_c070_2050b_05800_01050_1: The world doesn't have to change. There is no one "truth."
PID_c070_2050b_06000_01050_1: You have to accept it as it is...but still find the strength to stand up and face it.
PID_c070_2050b_06100_03220_1: Be quiet! Then...then, what did She work so hard for!?
